cases.name: a-pool-hands-a-whole-member-to-a-row
cases.description: A <pool> is a small table computed once, before the rows. A sequence draws ONE member per row through <gen type="pool">, and every field of that member is read as ${{Ref.field}}. The point is what cannot happen: two fields in a row always come from the same member, because a reference is one sequence and a sequence holds one value per row.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="pool" local="en" mode="memory"><pool name="P" count="3"><sequence name="a"><gen type="text" value="x,y,z"/></sequence><sequence name="b"><gen type="text" value="1,2,3"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="P"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.a}}${{R.b}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pool-is-drawn-from-a-derived-seed
cases.description: A pool draws from <seed>#pool:<Name>, not from the main stream, so adding one must leave every other column exactly where it was. These two columns are byte-identical to the same config with no pool in it — that is what this case pins.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="5" seed="derive" local="en" mode="memory"><pool name="P" count="4"><sequence name="n"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c,d"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="id"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="age"><gen type="number" value="18..90"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="P"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{id}},${{age}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pool-reference-filtered-by-a-column
cases.description: filter= narrows WHICH members a row may draw from — here to those whose c equals the row's own C. Unlike if=, it never leaves a cell empty: it substitutes a matching member, and no match at all is an error rather than a gap. The pool uses percent so the quota guarantees both values are present.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="8" seed="filt" local="en" mode="memory"><pool name="P" count="6"><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="N,S" percent="50,50"/></sequence><sequence name="who"><gen type="text" value="p,q,r,s,t,u" order="sequential"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="C"><gen type="text" value="N,S" percent="50,50"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="P" filter="c == C"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{C}}:${{R.c}}${{R.who}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pool-filter-is-an-expression-not-a-pair-of-names
cases.description: filter= takes the same expression language as if=, so !=, <, >, && and || all work. A bare word stays a string literal exactly as it does in if=, which this case relies on: `c != S` compares against the literal S, not against a column.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="8" seed="expr" local="en" mode="memory"><pool name="P" count="8"><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="N,S" percent="50,50"/></sequence><sequence name="k"><gen type="text" value="1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8" order="sequential"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="P" filter="c != S"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.c}}${{R.k}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-inside-a-pool-makes-the-members-differ
cases.description: A pool is a miniature <env>, so <uniq> inside one means what it means outside: these four members are four different (a, b) pairs. Nothing was written to make that work — a pool is built by the ordinary sequence machinery with the member count in place of the row count.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="20" seed="pooluniq" local="en" mode="memory"><pool name="P" count="4"><uniq><sequence name="a"><gen type="text" value="x,y" percent="50,50"/></sequence><sequence name="b"><gen type="text" value="1,2" percent="50,50"/></sequence></uniq></pool><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="P"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.a}}${{R.b}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pool-member-draws-from-another-pool
cases.description: A member of one pool draws a whole member of another, declared above it. The inner reference publishes no bare column — only `at.k` and `at.t` — so a row reads `${{R.at.k}}` and the clinic a doctor works at is fixed per MEMBER, not per row. The inner pool is built off its own derived seed, which is why the same pair travels together everywhere the doctor appears.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="pool" local="en"><pool name="C" count="2"><sequence name="k" uniq="true"><gen type="text" value="n,s"/></sequence><sequence name="t"><gen type="text" value="1,2"/></sequence></pool><pool name="D" count="3"><sequence name="a"><gen type="text" value="x,y,z"/></sequence><sequence name="at"><gen type="pool" value="C"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="D"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.a}}${{R.at.k}}${{R.at.t}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-filter-compares-the-way-loose-equality-does
cases.description: `field == Column` is bucketed rather than evaluated, and the bucket used to be keyed by raw text. A pool holding 01,02,03 against a column producing 1,2,3 was REFUSED by TDC225 as unmatchable, while the same filter with one term that changes nothing matched every row.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="p" local="en" mode="memory"><pool name="Codes" count="3"><sequence name="code"><gen type="text" value="01,02,03" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="label"><gen type="text" value="alpha,beta,gamma" order="sequential"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="Want"><gen type="text" value="1,2,3" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="Hit"><gen type="pool" value="Codes" filter="code == Want"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{Want}} -> ${{Hit.label}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: distinct-over-two-references-to-one-pool
cases.description: A config-level <distinct> around two references to the same <pool> is kept by member IDENTITY: no row hands both of them the same doctor. A reference holds a whole record, so there is no value to compare — the group compares WHICH MEMBER the row took. Before this worked the config was accepted and did nothing at all, and the run was byte for byte the same as one without the group.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="8" seed="clinic" local="en" mode="memory"><pool name="Doctors" count="4"><sequence name="name" uniq="true"><gen type="text" value="Adams,Brooks,Chase,Dunn"/></sequence></pool><distinct><sequence name="Duty"><gen type="pool" value="Doctors"/></sequence><sequence name="Seen"><gen type="pool" value="Doctors"/></sequence></distinct></env><block><line><data>${{Duty.name}}|${{Seen.name}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: distinct-over-references-composes-with-filter
cases.description: The repair draws from the candidates a filter= leaves standing, so both promises hold at once: every row's two doctors are different people AND both are in the department the row asked for. That is why the candidate SET is what the group works with, not just the pick.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="8" seed="clinic" local="en" mode="memory"><pool name="Doctors" count="6"><sequence name="name" uniq="true"><gen type="text" value="Adams,Brooks,Chase,Dunn,Ellis,Frost"/></sequence><sequence name="dept"><gen type="text" value="cardio,neuro" order="sequential"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="Want"><gen type="text" value="cardio,neuro"/></sequence><distinct><sequence name="A"><gen type="pool" value="Doctors" filter="dept == Want"/></sequence><sequence name="B"><gen type="pool" value="Doctors" filter="dept == Want"/></sequence></distinct></env><block><line><data>${{Want}}|${{A.name}}|${{B.name}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-over-two-references-to-one-pool
cases.description: A config-level <uniq> around references is one axis further out than <distinct>: no two ROWS take the same combination of members. Kept by rearranging the picks rather than redrawing, so each reference keeps its multiset and the fields follow — a field is a pure function of the member. Rows may still repeat a member within themselves; that is <distinct>'s job, not this one.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="8" seed="clinic" local="en" mode="memory"><pool name="Doctors" count="5"><sequence name="name" uniq="true"><gen type="text" value="Adams,Brooks,Chase,Dunn,Ellis"/></sequence></pool><uniq><sequence name="A"><gen type="pool" value="Doctors"/></sequence><sequence name="B"><gen type="pool" value="Doctors"/></sequence></uniq></env><block><line><data>${{A.name}}|${{B.name}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-distinct-template-list-inside-a-pool
cases.description: A pool member's repeated template of a plain pack with distinct="true". A plain pack is a list, laid out in equal shares like a text list — the streaming engine's road. The reference's in-memory engine drew each element instead, and in a pool, where no per-row path had narrowed the build to one row, every retry drew the same allergy and the run refused. Rust, Java and C# already laid it out; Python had copied the reference.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="5" seed="r6" local="en"><pool name="Pats" count="20"><sequence name="pid"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="allg"><gen type="template" value="medical.allergy" repeat="1..3" separator="; " distinct="true"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="P"><gen type="pool" value="Pats" filter="pid == _count"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{P.pid}}: ${{P.allg}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-switch-reads-a-field-of-a-pool-record
cases.description: <switch on="D.dno"> on a field of a record drawn from a pool. The reference ran it; the four ports refused it as TDC134, "not a field of D", looking the subject up among plain names only.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="Docs" count="4"><sequence name="dno"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="D"><gen type="pool" value="Docs"/></sequence><switch name="W" on="D.dno"><map>1:one, 2:two</map><default><data>many</data></default></switch></env><block><line><data>${{D.dno}} ${{W}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-switch-inside-a-pool-reads-a-field-a-member-drew
cases.description: The same inside a pool: a member draws a record from another pool and a <switch> member reads one of its fields. Rust, Java and C# did not publish the fields of a reference inside a pool at all.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="Docs" count="4"><sequence name="dno"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence></pool><pool name="Pats" count="4"><sequence name="pid"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="doc"><gen type="pool" value="Docs"/></sequence><switch name="W" on="doc.dno"><map>1:one, 2:two</map><default><data>many</data></default></switch></pool><sequence name="P"><gen type="pool" value="Pats" filter="pid == _count"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{P.pid}} ${{P.doc.dno}} ${{P.W}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-date-offset-measures-from-a-field-of-a-pool-record
cases.description: of="D.ddate": an offset from a date a pool record holds. The ports refused it as TDC240, "not a sequence declared above", because the field paths of a reference never entered the list of names declared above.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="Days" count="5"><sequence name="di"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="ddate"><gen type="date" from="2024-01-01" order="sequential" step="1d" format="YYYY-MM-DD"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="K"><gen type="text" value="1,2,3,4,5"/></sequence><sequence name="D"><gen type="pool" value="Days" filter="di == K"/></sequence><sequence name="B"><gen type="date" of="D.ddate" plus="-3..-1d" format="YYYY-MM-DD"/></sequence><assert each="D.di == K" says="x"/></env><block><line><data>${{D.ddate}} ${{B}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: each-walks-a-pool-record-by-record
cases.description: <line each="Pool"> prints one line per record of the pool, in pool order, and a record's fields read as ${{Pool.field}}. The walked name carries its positions: Pool._item counts from 1, Pool._first and Pool._last say whether this is the first or last line printed — which is what puts a comma between the members of a JSON array and not after the last one. A pool is the same on every row, so a two-row run prints it twice.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="each-pool" local="en" mode="memory"><pool name="Depts" count="3"><sequence name="id"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="name"><gen type="text" value="Cardiology,Neurology,Surgery" order="sequential"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="Id"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>row ${{Id}}</data></line><line each="Depts"><data>  ${{Depts._item}} ${{Depts.id}} ${{Depts.name}} first=${{Depts._first}} last=${{Depts._last}}</data><data if="!Depts._last">,</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: each-pool-reads-a-nested-record
cases.description: A pool field that draws from another pool is a record one level down, read as ${{Doctors.dept.name}} on a line walking Doctors. The old _item and _item_id built-ins still work on a pool line: both are the record's 1-based position.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="each-nested" local="en" mode="memory"><pool name="Depts" count="3"><sequence name="id"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="name"><gen type="text" value="Cardiology,Neurology,Surgery" order="sequential"/></sequence></pool><pool name="Doctors" count="6"><sequence name="id"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="last"><gen type="text" value="Adams,Baker,Clark,Davis,Evans,Foster" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="dept"><gen type="pool" value="Depts"/></sequence></pool></env><block><line each="Doctors"><data>${{_item}}/${{_item_id}} ${{Doctors.last}} works in ${{Doctors.dept.name}} (dept ${{Doctors.dept.id}})</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: each-pool-if-filters-records-and-positions-count-the-printed-ones
cases.description: The line's if= is asked of every record, with the record in scope. The positions count only the records it lets through, so Doctors._last is the last line PRINTED — the comma rule stays right even when the last record of the pool is filtered out.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="each-filter" local="en" mode="memory"><pool name="Depts" count="3"><sequence name="id"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="name"><gen type="text" value="Cardiology,Neurology,Surgery" order="sequential"/></sequence></pool><pool name="Doctors" count="6"><sequence name="id"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="last"><gen type="text" value="Adams,Baker,Clark,Davis,Evans,Foster" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="dept"><gen type="pool" value="Depts"/></sequence></pool></env><block><line><data>[</data></line><line each="Doctors" if="Doctors.dept.id == 1"><data>  ${{Doctors._item}}:${{Doctors.last}}@${{Doctors.dept.id}}</data><data if="!Doctors._last">,</data></line><line><data>]</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: each-pool-in-before-and-after
cases.description: A fixture line may walk a pool too, so a lookup table can be printed once, ahead of the rows, instead of once per row.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="each-fixture" local="en" mode="memory"><pool name="Depts" count="3"><sequence name="id"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="name"><gen type="text" value="Cardiology,Neurology,Surgery" order="sequential"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="Id"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><before><line><data>depts:</data></line><line each="Depts"><data>  ${{Depts.id}}=${{Depts.name}}</data></line></before><after><line each="Depts" if="Depts.id == 3"><data>end with ${{Depts.name}} last=${{Depts._last}}</data></line></after></env><block><line><data>row ${{Id}}</data></line></block></tdc>
